summary: U.S. Soccer officially named Emma Hayes the 10th full-time USWNT head coach on Nov. 14, 2023, after a search that began in August following the World Cup round-of-16 exit and Vlatko Andonovski's departure. Hayes will stay with Chelsea until the end of the season in May, so Twila Kilgore remains interim coach through the transition. The article covers the deal's details, a reported salary near $2 million per year, the tight run-up to the Paris Olympics, and what comes next for Chelsea.
one_line: U.S. Soccer hired Emma Hayes as USWNT coach, starting after her final Chelsea season in May 2024, with Twila Kilgore interim until then.
key_facts: Chelsea announced on Nov. 4, 2023 that Emma Hayes would leave at the end of the season to pursue a new opportunity outside the WSL and club football; U.S. Soccer made her appointment official on Tuesday, Nov. 14.
Hayes will be the 10th full-time USWNT head coach and previously won six WSL titles with Chelsea.
Sporting director Matt Crocker made the final hiring decision after a search that began in August, following the USWNT's round-of-16 World Cup exit and Vlatko Andonovski's departure.
Tony Gustavsson, head coach of Australia, was also on the final shortlist, and both he and Hayes flew to the U.S. for interviews.
The federation reportedly checked on Sarina Wiegman's availability, though she said she was happy with England and had a contract until 2025.

The main concession by U.S. Soccer was the start date: Hayes stays exclusively with Chelsea through the WSL and Champions League seasons, possibly until May 25, and will not work with the USWNT in international windows.
U.S. Soccer owes Chelsea no compensation, and Hayes plans to move to Chicago in 2024 and eventually to Atlanta, where a combined headquarters and training facility is planned.

Hayes is expected to earn close to $2 million per year, making her the highest-paid women's football coach in the world; Berhalter earned $1.6 million (including $300,000 in bonuses) from April 2021 to March 2022, and Andonovski $446,495.
Hayes will have only two camps, including four friendlies, before the Paris Olympics, with 18 days with the team across windows May 27–June 4 and July 8–16; the Olympic tournament starts July 25.
Interim coach Twila Kilgore will lead through May and stay on as a permanent assistant under Hayes.
Hayes cited her five-year-old son Harry and leaving at the top as key reasons for leaving; her father died the previous month.
Chelsea's announcement was made early because the club feared the news was leaking; the U.S. Soccer board approved the selection late on Nov. 4 before the contract was finalized.
Assistant Denise Reddy, a friend of 20 years, is likely to follow Hayes to the U.S., while general manager Paul Green will stay at Chelsea.
Chelsea faces Real Madrid in its first Champions League group-stage match the day after the article.
